direction: Start with a striking but natural full-outfit view; keep the model and garment visible.
Use one relaxed, realistic model movement to show the garment's actual cut, fit and overall silhouette.
Move closer to a genuinely visible print, seam, sleeve, hem or fabric detail; do not invent texture or alter the pattern.
Show one category-appropriate step, gentle turn or natural fabric movement without exaggerated posing or wind.
Settle on a clean full-outfit view with the garment unchanged and room for optional selected hook/CTA text.
Open on the actual drape and overall styling, then show the full visible arrangement.
Use a small natural head or shoulder movement while keeping the wrap and folds consistent.
Show only visible folds, edging, print or texture; do not change the wrap, colour or fabric.
Make a gentle three-quarter camera adjustment to show the existing drape from a plausible angle.
Return to a clear, steady view of the same styling with room for optional selected hook/CTA text.
Open at a low three-quarter angle with the complete shoe or pair clearly visible.
If a wearer is selected, show a short natural step on a flat surface; otherwise keep the shoes grounded and stationary.
Highlight only the visible upper, fastening, sidewall or sole edge; never force an unseen angle.
Show a small, believable shift or two-step walk only if appropriate, preserving shoe shape and foot contact.
Hold a clean view of the unchanged pair or product arrangement with room for optional selected hook/CTA text.
Open on the bag's clearest recognizable silhouette, with all visible straps and handles in frame.
Show the complete bag at a believable scale in the selected setting; do not add contents or accessories.
Move close to one visible seam, handle, clasp or hardware detail only if present.
If the scene calls for it, show one natural lift or carry using an existing handle or strap; otherwise move the camera only.
Return to the same complete bag and hold a stable frame with room for optional selected hook/CTA text.
Open with a clean, recognizable view of the actual package and keep its label and shape consistent.
Show the whole product in a tidy, relevant setting; do not add extra containers or applicators.
Highlight a genuinely visible package or product texture detail without inventing ingredients, shade or efficacy.
Show only a small, plausible use action if the selected product supports it; otherwise use a restrained close-up.
Finish with the original product clearly framed and room for optional selected hook/CTA text.
Open on the actual food or drink with natural, appetizing light; do not add toppings or ingredients.
Show the complete original serving and packaging, where present.
Make a gentle close-up of visible texture, crumb, surface or liquid; preserve the actual appearance.
Use one plausible serving or pouring action only if supported by the product and scene; avoid exaggerated effects.
Return to the real serving or package and hold a clean final composition with room for optional selected hook/CTA text.
Open on a recognizable three-quarter view of the unchanged device.
Show the complete device and any supplied components without adding cables or accessories.
Move close only to a control, port, screen or button that is actually visible; keep screen content unchanged.
Show one simple action the named product genuinely supports; do not invent compatibility, specifications or functions.
Finish with a stable, complete device view and room for optional selected hook/CTA text.
